title: Primordial Serpents
snippet:
Kaathe resides in the darkness of the Abyss, but seems to be more involved in the affairs of Lordran than Frampt. Kaathe gave the Four Kings the art of lifedrain and consequently founded the Darkwraith covenant. He also seems to have tricked the residents of Oolacile into uncovering the corpse of Manus, driving him mad in the process. This sparked the spread of the Abyss, transforming the townsfolk into monstrous beings whose humanity has run wild, akin to Manus.

In the ending of Dark Lord, ten additional primordial serpents are seen, whose names are unknown. They appear to want to serve the newly-appointed Dark Lord, and possibly usher in the Age of Dark. An interesting note in this ending is that Kaathe states that both himself and Frampt will serve the Chosen Undead, disregarding any actions the player has taken before reaching this point, like placing the Lordvessel with Frampt instead of Kaathe, which would make the latter refuse to cooperate with the player, and vice-versa.

title: Undead Dragon
snippet:
Undead Dragon -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : In an interview with **PlayStation.blog**, Miyazaki said that the Dragon Zombie was designed as one of few survivor of the ancient dragons that went mad".
It's unclear why these dragons are undead, as the Curse of the Undead normally affects only humans. They may be "survivors" of the war against the Everlasting Dragons, reanimated unintentionally by Nito's deadly plague, or kept "alive" by Dragons' inborn vitality.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
In The Duke's Archives the Chosen Undead confronts Seath the Scaleless, an albino dragon who betrayed the Ancient Dragons and won Lord Gwyn´s trust. During their first encounter, the Chosen Undead is unable to cause any harm to Seath and is captured. Seath imprisons the Chosen Undead inside his prison tower where the player cannot warp out from. Despite the inconveniences, the Chosen Undead eventually escapes.

Later on, the Chosen Undead learns from Big Hat Logan that Seath is immortal due to an ancient artifact known as the Primordial Crystal, an old relic that Seath stole from the Ancient Dragons. The Chosen Undead then departs to the Crystal Cave, where the artifact lies, and shatters it. This annuls Seath's immortality, allowing the Chosen Undead to slay him.

Archive Tower Cell Key -  Dark Souls - item - general_information

title: Lothric
snippet: In his later years, dismayed by failures to find a worthy Champion, Oceiros developed a fascination for dragons that sent him into his descent into madness, eventually turning to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives. Here Oceiros found the heretical worship of the white dragon Seath, becoming deeply engrossed in it to the point where he wore a dragonscale ring and had his army use shields decorated with a "white dragon", while giving his royal guard magic rings that enhanced sorcery. By now lost in his madness, Oceiros became known as the "Consumed King"; many assassins were sent to kill him to remove him from power, but he managed to ward off the threat, attributing his salvation to the divine protection of the dragon scale.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet: theories : It is possible that the humanoid creatures that emerged underground and found the four Lord Souls are an evolution of the dragons over countless years. In fact, after the appearance of the First Flame and the souls, life became possible. The primordial immortal dragons began to mutate like Seath the Scaleless and Black Dragon Kalameet, and reproduced and evolved into different creatures with different characteristics and appearances such as wyverns and serpents. In the depths of the Tomb of the Giants it is in fact possible to find Skeletal Beasts: giant skeletons with bestial behavior that walk on four legs, with in particular a small tail at the end of their spinal column. In these primordial catacombs there are also Giant Skeletons that are able to walk upright and use weapons, but retaining traces of a tail in their bones. These two specimens highlight how those who inhabited the catacombs in very ancient times were creatures initially similar to beasts with tails

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The ghostly hands that emerge from the tomes in the Grand Archives in *Dark Souls III* closely resemble those of Seath; not only visually, but also functionally, as they cause curse build-up in those who come too close, similar to Seath's Curse Beam attacks.
Seath's character is an homage to the dragon god of the same name in FromSoftware's King's Field series for the original Playstation. The Souls series is often referred to as the spiritual successor to King's Field.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : When first encountered in The Duke's Archives, he regenerates health extremely quickly due to the power of Primordial Crystal, effectively making him invincible.. He inevitably kills the player. Loss of souls and humanity can be avoided by wearing a Ring of Sacrifice, but if he kills the player through Curse, then a Rare Ring of Sacrifice is needed to avoid penalties. In addition, it is possible to travel back through the fog door to avoid being killed by Seath, however can still go through the fog wall after exiting. Regardless, the player must be killed by Seath in order to progress.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath eventually sired a humanoid hybrid daughter, Shira. Although the mother is never stated explicitly, Shira is both "one whose veins coarse with royal blood", and a "descendant of Gods", making her likely mother Seath's spouse who was a relative of Gwyn.
 Shira became the sworn knight and personal handmaiden to Princess Filianore, Gwyn's last daughter, and the two, together with the dragon Darkeater Midir, would be forever sent away to the Ringed City, the hidden city Gwyn gifted to the humans who helped him end the Age of Ancients, so that the three would keep the Dark within at bay. Shira would remain in the Ringed City for the rest of her life, dutifully guarding Filianore over countless ages, although she would always take pride in being Seath's daughter.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : It is incredibly likely that the Duke mentioned by Shira is none other than Seath the Scaleless himself. For one, he is the only prominent duke who is ever mentioned as part of the age of the gods, which would explain why Shira speaks of her parentage to a duke as if it were self-explanatory. Another clue may come from the pearl lodged in her crown, which was harvested from the Man Eater Clams. These creatures were found nesting in the Crystal Cave, part of Seath's domain, as well as the primordial Ash Lake, a place tied to the dragons.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Another possible daughter of Seath was Crossbreed Priscilla, a half-dragon hybrid whose dragon attributes are reminiscent of him; as she is outright described as a bastard, she would have been conceived out of wedlock. Priscilla was feared by the other gods and treated as an abomination due to her Lifehunt powers and unnatural origin. Eventually she was drawn away into the cold and lonely Painted World of Ariamis, trapped within a great canvas.

Seath seemingly had little interest in politics or pleasure, choosing to immerse himself in research of the scales of immortality that the ancient dragons possessed but he lacked. His Archives became a magnificent pool of tomes and knowledge, the fruits of Seath's superior wisdom and unsound fixation over achieving the immortality that was denied to him at birth.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point, the Four Lords who had found immense Lord Souls and built their civilizations underground emerged to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world for themselves. Seath decided to betray his race to ally with Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, and help the Lords in the war. He was instrumental in the gods' eventual victory, and the triumphant Lords would exterminate much of the Ancient Dragons, cementing their rule. Seath would also pillage the Ancient Dragons' sacred treasure, the Primordial Crystal, the centerpiece of his efforts to achieve immortality.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_war_of_fire 
 the_war_of_fire : With their new found power the Lords challenged the dominion of the Everlasting Dragons over the World. The Lords allied with one of the dragons, Seath the Scaleless, who sought the immortal scales of the dragons and thus betrayed his own kind. A very long and destructive war was begun by the Lords and their amassed armies. Gwyn used his powerful bolts to peel their stone scales, while the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great firestorms against them and finally the Gravelord Nito unleashed a miasma of death upon the dragons. The war was won by the Lords and the dragons were defeated. A golden Age of Fire begun as the World rebuilt under the new rule of the now as deities perceived Lords.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Following the death of their creator, multiple moon butterflies survived over the centuries, migrating to Drangleic and mutating into lesser Great Moths and developing poisoning abilities. They remained rare and mysterious creatures that appeared only on full-moon nights in winter, and whose larvae were never once spotted. Other creations of Seath that reached Drangleic included Manscorpion Tark and Scorpioness Najka: Two of Seath's many experiments on humans, the pale dragon's crossbreeding experiments had seemingly cursed their souls into being together. The two were well aware of being the product of Seath's madness and his obsessive attempt to achieve immortality.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Studying the sorceries and knowledge brought to the Archives by the Crystal Sages, Oceiros would find himself walking the same path as Big Hat Logan, one that led to enlightenment only to be followed by madness. The king, in his deep delusions, believed he had to become a dragon himself in order to produce an heir strong enough to link the Flame. His mad plans would find support from Pontiff Sulyvahn, who began experimenting with transforming humans into pale dragons. Despite the large number of failures and abominations that presented only a faded fragment of the dragons' strength, the experiments were eventually successful and Oceiros managed to transform himself into a scaleless dragon resembling Seath, albeit an imperfect and distorted one, even obtaining the sorcery of Seath's crystal breath.

title: Lore
snippet:
Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

Seath, who became obsessed with his research and experiments, amassed countless tomes and was eventually driven mad - at least, how normal people see it - by his research, becoming the founder of sorcery.

At least a thousand years pass and the events of "Dark Souls" begin to unfold...

title: Dragon
snippet: Oceiros, the Consumed King, was formerly the King of Lothric, later becoming obsessed with Seath the Scaleless' work and seeking to become more powerful using his royal blood. With the aid of the scholars of the Grand Archives, he discovered the research made by Logan, who himself was inspired by Seath. Much like Logan, Oceiros was driven insane by the work of the paledrake and somehow transformed into a malformed abomination, somewhat reminiscent of Seath. He has survived many assassination attempts, which he claims is due to the divine protection of the dragon scale.

title: Timeline
snippet:
----
Seath The Scaleless betrays his kind and reveals dragon scales give dragons their immortality
Gwyn uses lightning to destroy their scales and make them vulnerable
Nito unleashed a miasma of death and disease, rotting the Archtrees and infecting the dragons
Seath steals the Primordial Crystal and swears allegiance to the newcomers
The majority of dragons and most Archtrees are destroyed, save for lesser dragons and several survivors
One such survivor is the Stone Dragon, founder of The Path of the Dragon
Some Dragons are chosen to serve a purpose under Gwyn's new rule: Midir is raised and trained since its young state to serve as a devourer of dark energy, able to carry its duty at the service of light forever while staying (theoretically) uncorrupted

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Through their successful alliance against the Everlasting Dragons, Seath became a close friend to the Lord of Sunlight and was amply rewarded for his indispensable contributions to the war. He was wed into Gwyn's family as his son-in-law, inducting him into the nobility of the Gods, and was bestowed the honorific of "Duke". Gwyn further gifted Seath a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the Royal Archives, an enormous library towering above Anor Londo, which contained all the knowledge available to the city of the gods, leaving the dragon the freedom to do his own research; in time, the archives became so synonymous with Seath that they became known as "The Duke's Archives" instead.

title: Dragon
snippet:
According to interviews with Miyazaki, the Ancient Dragons are half-living, half-element, and do not feel pain due to them being "beyond human understanding". They are mineral-based lifeforms existing since before humanity's emergence, yet the very emergence of life was capable of corrupting them and causing them to be warped by emotions and desires, to the point where their very bodies adapt and retrogress in pursuit of their survival, such as the Gaping Dragon being warped by greed and the desire to eat.

Seath and the Stone Dragon prove that these beings were capable of higher reasoning and could understand other species' language to at least some degree, via their known contributions to the world (the former, Seath, being the founder of soul sorcery, along with creating the techniques of forging weapons from powerful souls according to Weaponsmith Ornifex).

It is common for the tails of Dragons to be cut off and used in the forging of powerful weapons.

 dark_souls_iii : By the era of Lothric, Seath was still widely considered the "pale dragon" of legends even by the sorcerers of Vinheim, though his crystal sorceries were all but consigned to legend.

There were some who still upheld Seath's legacy: The Crystal Sages, twin scholars who considered themselves the spiritual successors of the legendary grand sage Logan, came to possess the Crystal Scroll containing the sorceries and research of the pale dragon, which lead to Logan's records of Crystal Sorcery. The two sages were thus able to carry on this branch of sorcery, allowing them to replicate Logan's discoveries that utilize the power of crystals to their fullest as a medium for souls thanks to his "enlightenment" in the Regal Archives of Seath.

title: Dragon
snippet:
It is common for the tails of Dragons to be cut off and used in the forging of powerful weapons.

Although the Dragons predate souls and originally did not bear them, over time some would come to possess souls of their own such as Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon, even ones that existed and died just after the Age of Ancients such as the Ancient Dragon. In fact, dragon bones, when imbued with the power of the soul, can be used as an appropriate core to powerful constructs like the Iron Golem, who guards Sen's Fortress and slays the countless heroes seeking Anor Londo. Petrified Dragon Bone is said to house great power.

A Dragon Tooth from an Everlasting Dragon is considered harder than stone and as solid as a boulder, and stated to never break; Havel the Rock would use one as a great club. Merely holding one will grant the user resistance to both fire and magic, suggesting that the Everlasting Dragons had a similar if greater resistance, in contrast to their weakness to lightning.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At the culmination of his quest, Seath was able to achieve what he had always sought: immortality through the Primordial Crystal. By connecting his body and soul to the powerful crystal, the pale dragon gained insulation from death, so that no mortal blow could affect him and his wounds would close promptly, as long as the crystal was intact. His very breath became a powerful crystal breath that emitted a lethal curse.

Seath was born with unique characteristics compared to the other archdragons, lacking the rock scales that made his brethren immortal. In addition, Seath's pale and deformed body was infused with the magical power of moonlight, through the study of which he created weapons that catalyzed it.

title: Gods
snippet:
Havel the Rock, a battlefield compatriot of Gwyn who fought at his side against the Everlasting Dragons and inspired many warriors who wore similar equipment. He is referred to as a "bishop" , and is clearly part of the faith of the Way of White, as there were even "priests of Havel" and miracles recalling his tales, although whether he was actually deified, or part of Gwyn's species, is unclear.
Seath, an Everlasting Dragon who sided with Gwyn against his own species. After the war, he was granted Dukedom, married a woman in Gwyn's family, and came to be regarded as the Godfather of sorcery, although he was seemingly not deified.
Many Silver Knights since the Age of Ancients served Lord Gwyn and the other Old Gods of Anor Londo, well into the events of *Dark Souls III*. Their origins and species are never clearly explained.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Being the grandfather of Sorcery, Seath is extremely resistant to Magic damage, so it would be wise to try to use a different element when combating him.

When trying to obtain the Moonlight Greatsword it is best to attack the tip of the tail, as the area around midway through the tail is considered his body. Thus dealing damage to this area will not help in acquiring the Moonlight Greatsword.

A good strategy for acquiring it is when Seath himself breaks the Primordial Crystal. Wait behind the crystal until Seath starts to rear up his head for any of the Curse Beam attacks. Just before he fires it, start sprinting left or right around the sides and towards his tail. Seath will break the crystal and stun himself, giving the player ample opportunity to attack his tail three to four times. Make sure Seath's tail isn't clipping in the wall before trying.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan soon leaves Firelink Shrine after the Lordvessel has been obtained. He is then jailed in The Duke's Archives. Logan explains that he is there to study Seath the Scaleless and his magic. After freeing him with the Archive Tower Giant Cell Key, players can find Logan in an ancillary library close to the third bonfire in The Duke's Archives, where he sells Crystal Sorceries as well as his prior spells. Alternatively, if not freed by you by Seath's defeat, he will free himself and move to the library.

Unfortunately, Logan's infatuation with Seath's magic eventually drives him insane after Seath has been defeated and his entire stock of spells has been purchased. Speaking with him again, after the above conditions are met, will cause him to move to the large chamber where Seath the Scaleless was first encountered and become hostile.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: The tide would turn in the Lords' favor when Seath, a pale dragon born without the scales of his kind, betrayed the dragons to ally with Gwyn, and pillaged their Primordial Crystal. Seath's lack of scales coupled with his vulnerability provided the Lords with a key piece of information: that the scales of his brethren were the source of their immortality. Gwyn thus used his Great Soul to manipulate the light of the sun, transforming rays of sunlight into lightning, a form of energy capable of penetrating dragon scales. Meeting the dragons in battle, Gwyn used his spears of sunlight to peel apart the dragons' scales, while his knights employed lightning-infused weapons to similar effect. The Witch of Izalith and her daughters weaved great firestorms, destroying the archtrees and burning the dragons; while Nito unleashed a miasma of death, rotting the archtrees and infecting the dragons. Gwyn's eldest son would also take part in the war with his father, killing several dragons with his

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The pale dragon's experiments were successful in animating Crystal Golems with souls and infusing Undead Soldiers with crystals. To adequately supply his research, the cave that housed his Primordial Crystal was gradually crowded with crystals, nearly overtaking the Archive's inner gardens. Seath also created the soul of the Moonlight Butterflies, mystical creatures that emitted crystallic power and Seath's moonlight as sorceries. Seath also managed to crystallize his own magical power of moonlight, creating a Greatsword that catalyzed it.

As a nobleman on par with the gods, Seath also had personal servants. His Channelers, trained sorcerers that became his eyes, hands, and feet, would reach and see what the dragon could not, and helped him in his research. The Channelers wore outfits representing Seath, with the six eyes on their helms meant to "compensate for Seath's lack of sight"; the nature of his lack of sight, and when he became impaired, are unknown.

title: Man Serpent (Lore)
snippet: Ultimately, they might simply be the result of various experiments related to dragons or the Man Serpents, either conducted by Seath himself, who wasn't unfamiliar with merging two different beings together to further his research as evidenced by the existence of Manscorpion Tark and Scorpioness Najka, or by the Bastille Lord himself, their former master.

title: Ocelotte
snippet: In his later years, now consumed by his continuous failures, Oceiros became fascinated by dragons and began to slide into madness, eventually turning to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives where he founded the heretical faith in the white dragon Seath. Continuing to study the sorceries and knowledge contained in the Archives and brought by the Crystal Sages to Lothric, Oceiros found himself walking the same path as Big Hat Logan, reaching the same level of "enlightenment" as him and then going completely mad. The king, in his deep delusions, believed he had to become a dragon himself in order to produce an heir strong enough to link the Flame. Oceiros eventually managed to transform himself into a scaleless dragon form, albeit an imperfect and distorted one, even obtaining the sorcery of Seath's crystal breath

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Equipment load under 25% is highly recommended to cut his tail.
Lure Seath as close as possible to the crystal. It is ideal to kite Seath close to one of the walls, so that when he attacks with his breath, you have plenty of room to move around his other side. Once Seath is close enough to you he will pause and begin his breath attack; immediately run behind Seath. Run to his left side (your right), as he breathes his crystal breath from his right to his left. Seath will destroy the crystal with his own breath attack and be stunned temporarily. Without locking on to him, target the tip of his back (middle) tail and attack it while two-handing your highest damage weapon or using fast strong spells.
Use weapons that have vertical slash when two-handed: katanas, straightswords, greatswords, ultra greatswords, etc. Slash the tip once or twice, then run away. Provoke him to attack with his crystal breath, run to his tail, slash once or twice again, then repeat.

This would also explain the immense amount of gifts that Gwyn gave to the white dragon including the Archives of the Gods, a political position in his empire, a woman from his family and a fragment of his Lord's soul.

title: Dragon
snippet: The Dragons' iconic characteristic, their stone scales that gave them immortality, was implied to have a strong connection with their own form to the point where Dragons and their scales were considered "inseparable", though the exact truth of this is undetermined. However, their transcendent apostles, who seek the perpetuity of the ancient dragons, have crossed the very ends of the earth to find them and offer them up to rise above their petty corporeal existence and become Dragons. Touching a Ancient Dragon Scale is said to give a person a glimpse into the abyss.

snippet:

 dark_souls_ii : In the region and times of Drangleic, Seath's name had been forgotten, merely referred to as an "Old One"; the legend of a pale dragon was nonetheless passed on in various locales, even if each account was fragmentary. His Moonlight Sword that shone like the brilliant rays of the moon and was born from his white being had become a thing of the oldest legends, rarely spoken of. The smithing techniques of Seath that used souls to create artifacts were preserved by a clan of Crow Demons, though they remembered the dragon only as a white grotesque being that existed in the distant past.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - dragon_war 
 dragon_war : With the strength given to them by the Lord Souls, the three waged a war on the Everlasting Dragons. They were joined by Seath, a scaleless albino dragon that pillaged the Primordial Crystal from them as well and turned on his own kind.

To combat the dragons, Gwyn released grand bolts of light so powerful that they stripped the dragons of their stone scales. With her daughters, the Witch wove firestorms that incinerated the land. Once this was done, Nito arrived for the killing blow by releasing the miasma of death upon the dragons. Soon the dragons were defeated - but not gone - and the Age of Fire began.
Even after the war, Gwyn was known to have sporting hunts of those descended from the dragons.

title: Old Ones
snippet: The Writhing Ruin is described as an ancient entity whose influence in Brightstone Cove Tseldora made the inhabitants be consumed in the search for “that which they lacked”. Furthermore, Manscorpion Tark, who congratulates the player for “defeating his master” after Freja is killed (referring to the Writhing Ruin possesing her) describes his master as a being “born with a fatal flaw, hateful of those that had what he lacked, creator of strange creatures and eroded by solitude and madness". This is a perfect definition of Seath the Scaleless search for immortality. Other correlations are Scorpioness Najka, who has the same creator of Tark, being able to use sorceries, the same crystal theme aesthetic both the Writhing Ruin and Seath have and that the word “Writhing” means a squirming cortorcion similar to the movements of tentacles.

title: Dragon
snippet: description : The Dragons have a few different names throughout the series; **Everlasting Dragons**, **Ancient Dragons**, **Archdragons**, or simply **Dragons**. From what can be glimpsed in the opening, the Everlasting Dragons were towering beings with a skin covered both by stone scales and bristly dark fur. Their head sported two straight horns and a mouth bearing two rows of sharp teeth on both jaws. Their back ended in a long and heavy tail but they were still able to fly thanks to their wings (which often came in two pairs), leathery and clawed like those of a bat. Appropriately for creatures that lived in a world of fog and penumbra, their two eyes had vertical slotted pupils (this kind of eye is the symbol of both the Path of the Dragon and the Dragon Remnants). Aside from these reptilian features, the Everlasting Dragons' body was a lot less bestial than that of their descendants and kin: their arms didn't end in claws but in four-digited prehensile hands while their torso,

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Transitioning from its disguised to active state will take some time and is a perfect opportunity to finish it off if the player is capable of dealing enough damage.
If one is patient enough, it is possible to observe a Mimic breathing and moving slightly as their idle animation. They'll even stretch their arms and legs out in rare occurrences.
Throwing a Lloyd's Talisman at a Mimic will cause it to open its mouth, allowing players to safely retrieve items from it without having to fight it. This can be done even if the mimic is hostile, in which case it'll sit back down.
It used to be possible to kill every Mimic in the game and not get the Symbol of Avarice. However, Patch 1.05 made the final Mimic in The Duke's Archives (the one in front of the exit to the grove of Crystal Golems) a guaranteed source for a Symbol of Avarice upon killing it.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Mimics disguise themselves as chests, waiting for victims to try to open them. When a player attempts to do so, Mimics will proceed to chomp on them in a special grab move, causing heavy damage.

If Mimics are hurt before they can grab a player, they reveal a large, lolling tongue and lines of finger-bone teeth, followed by the arms and legs. Once upright they will begin to aggressively pursue their prey. Mimics are fast, tough, and deal high damage; they can easily kill the unprepared.

In order to determine the difference between a Mimic and Chest, the most direct visual cue one can get is by looking at the chain connected to the right side of the chest. If the chain is wrapped in a circle then the chest is safe, if the chain is straightened out then it's a Mimic. The mimic chest will also do a long, slow breath with its lid slightly rising up and down once every 17 seconds.

title: Mimic
snippet:
In Co-op it is actually possible to save another player from a mimic. When the other player opens the mimic, if one acts quickly and attacks the mimic while it is still opening, it will instead stand up and initiate normal combat.
Mimics can't climb ladders.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : The mimic originates in the original *Advanced Dungeons & Dragons* *Monster Manual* (1977). In that sourcebook, they are carnivorous shapechangers able to take the form of any solid stone or wooden object, though they are most commonly depicted as treasure chests. Mimics have since appeared in numerous video game RPGs.
**According to *Dungeons & Dragons* editor Tim Kask, Gary Gygax created the mimic to foil players who checked for traps before opening treasure chests. The result, just as in Dark Souls, was to instill a sense of paranoia among players opening chests.
A Mimic's teeth are actually finger bones.
Mimics have a unique death animation if they die before being awakened.
If the player watches closely, a Mimic lying in wait will slowly open its lid, and then slowly close it.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : These creatures were once part of the great clan of the Gods but at one point they committed the sin of "greed". For this they were banished and cursed, resulting into their heads transforming into an imitation of treasure chests. They would became known as Mimics and spread across the world, simulating chests to trick and devour adventurers or becoming deadly defense mechanisms to protect peculiar artifacts.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Mimics** are special enemies encountered in *Dark Souls*. They will initially remain on the same spot, non-hostile and disguised as item chests until the player either opens them, which triggers a strong special grab, or hits them, which turns them hostile. There is a fixed number of nine Mimics found throughout the game, always in the same spots.

The usually-valuable treasure they contain can be obtained by either opening them safely using a Lloyd's Talisman or killing them. They do not respawn when killed, and in all versions of the game post Patch 1.05, the Mimic located in the Duke's Archives always drops the previously-rare Symbol of Avarice headware upon death.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - theory 
 theory : It's possible that the curse "imposed" to them is actually a mutation caused by their greed

The Gaping Dragon, the Crow Demons, the Covetous Demon, and many other beings attest that strong emotions can warp one's body. It's therefore plausible that the Mimic were molded by greed, and that their mutation had been attributed to divine punishment due to a mistaken interpretation.

title: Mimic
snippet:
Mimic -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategies 
 strategies : A good way to quickly dispatch a Mimic is to land as much damage before it is fully upright. Using attacks such as the two handed leaping attack or a powerful spell is the best way to weaken it as much as possible due to the long transformation.
When the mimic is active, it will move quickly and deal high damage if it hits. In particular, its spinning kick deals high knockback and damage.
If a Mimic is able to start chewing on the player, the player is most assuredly going to die. However, rapidly pressing the weak attack buttons will allow the player to escape.
All of the Mimic's attacks except for the standing kick, which must either be blocked or dodged, will miss if the player positions him/herself close against the Mimic.
Once a Mimic is awake, Lloyd's Talismans can still lull them, allowing the player to heal themselves or finish it off.

title: Avelyn
snippet:

 small_notes_small : #Begin by rotating the stairs so that the lower part is connected to the side closest to the item chest.

title: Avelyn
snippet: Like all crossbows, you cannot aim down sights so the Binoculars can help with aiming. With the Binoculars, line the target up in the exact center of the screen. Change to Avelyn without moving the camera, then fire. Despite its unique nature, Avelyn is considered a standard crossbow and can be upgraded as such. Like all crossbows Avelyn does not scale off any stats though upgrading increases base damage, if infusing the AR of elemental bolts is added to the elemental AR of the infusion, which can be beneficial. Use ammo types that elementally match the infusion when possible and factor in enemy resistances when choosing an infusion and/or ammo type.

title: Avelyn
snippet:
Avelyn -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The fact that it shoots three bolts at once means that it takes three times as much ammunition as any other crossbow in the game, so make those shots count. If only a single bolt hits an enemy most of the time, it's better to use the Heavy Crossbow instead, as it is lighter and has higher damage-per-bolt ratio.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : A **Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard** are two unique Soul items in *Dark Souls*. They are used by the Chosen Undead to partially satiate the Lordvessel together with two full Lord Souls, and gain access to the Kiln of the First Flame.

The Four Kings and Seath the Scaleless each own a Bequeathed Shard, which differ in lore from Lord Souls as they are only fragments of Gwyn's own Lord Soul, although even these fragments remain immensely powerful.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - backstory 
 backstory : Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards differ from Lord Souls in that they are shards of the Lord Soul of Gwyn. The owners of these shards were awarded them because Gwyn recognized the talent of the Four Kings of New Londo as leaders, and because Seath aided the Lords in the war of the Dragons.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the term (Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, thus stating how Seath had become part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet: **While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift thus allowing the dragon a more close connection to the family of the monarch.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : is a character in *Dark Souls*. First met in Sen's Fortress, from which he relocates to Firelink Shrine, he is a merchant of advanced sorceries, including new ones upon following his questline into The Duke's Archives.

Voiced by Ian Thompson in his final role before his passing in 2022, Logan is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II* and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*, although *Dark Souls II* refers to him as an unnamed "master sorcerer" due to his name being forgotten in Drangleic.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Master Logan was a famous Sorcerer and a royal member of the Vinheim Dragon School before he turned Undead about one hundred years ago. His nickname stems from the gigantic hat he wore which completely hid his face; he used it to block the noise and stares from those around him in order to focus his thoughts. His weapon was once an ordinary catalyst employed by the Sorcerers of Vinheim, but it has since been strengthened due to lengthy use over time. His sage robe, called prototype, meaning it goes back the School foundation of the Dragon School, therefore the School was founded around the times Logan was alive.

Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Big Hat Logan seems to prefer sitting down in a meditative position, except for the first encounter when he's in a hanging jail cage.
If you get the Man-Serpent leaning against the wall next to the cage he is in, It will break, meaning you don't need to get the boulder trap to break it, with careful planning.
Logan shares many similarities with Sage Freke from *Demon's Souls*. Both are first found trapped in cages and rescued by the player. Both are preceded by apprentices looking for them, have an unhealthy fascination with magic, and are found sitting in the main hub area.
Rickert of Vinheim mentions to the player that Big Hat Logan is famous in Vinheim; however, he also mentions that Logan was from "a hundred years ago". Either Logan has remained sane for as long as he has been undead, or time warping in Lordran has brought Logan to a time where one does not belong.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
When Logan is encountered hostile, he is not hollowed, but was driven insane in a more "traditional" sense. All other NPCs appear in their charred, undead forms when they attack players after hollowing.
If the player dies fighting against Big Hat Logan while in Seath's arena, the player will respawn in the prison as if they were killed by Seath himself, which underlines that Logan became just as mad as Seath.
Logan's Tin Crystallization Catalyst is actually 結晶の錫杖 ("Crystall Staff"). 錫杖 (khakkhara), is a ringed staff used by Buddhist monks. This implies that Logan venerated Seath as a God.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Big Hat Logan is first encountered in Sen's Fortress. His cage is hidden behind a wall, which can be destroyed by manipulating the iron ball trap mechanism, using a powerful enough weapon, or goading the sleeping man-serpent guard to attack the wall. After freeing him with either the Cage Key or Master Key, Big Hat Logan thanks the player and later retreats to Firelink Shrine. There, he accompanies Griggs of Vinheim and offers to sell the player advanced Sorceries.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

He is also the creator of Homing Soulmass, a sinister spell similar to Pursuers and therefore closer to dark sorceries, which enlights a more shady side of Logan. Griggs affirms that Logan has not concern for others, and that he is an unreasonable and troublesome man.

In his attempt to reach Anor Londo, presumably to gain access to The Duke's Archives and its vast store of endless knowledge, he became imprisoned in Sen's Fortress, where he first encounters the Chosen Undead.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Big Hat Logan has a repertoire of dangerous Sorceries, including Soul Spear and Homing Soulmass. If attacked later in the game, he also possesses their augmented crystal variants. However, he is fairly fragile and can be killed before he deals too much damage.

If killed when encountered in Sen's Fortress or Firelink Shrine, he will **not** drop anything.

title: Broken Pendant
snippet:
Broken Pendant -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : The** Broken Pendant** is a key item in *Dark Souls*. It is exclusive to the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC.

title: Broken Pendant
snippet:
Broken Pendant -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : The pendant is mentioned in the description of the Soul of Manus as an item of great importance and the reason for his descent into insanity.

title: Broken Pendant
snippet:
Broken Pendant -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : Dropped by a respawning Crystal Golem located near the beginning of The Duke's Archives. The Golem will only drop the pendant if Dusk of Oolacile has been rescued from within the Golden Crystal Golem, which can be found in an alcove past the Hydra in Darkroot Basin. It will only drop if the player talked to Dusk after rescuing her or if Dusk was killed.

The pendant can be obtained even if the player has killed the Golem prior to rescuing Dusk.

title: Broken Pendant
snippet:
Broken Pendant -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Possessing the Broken Pendant will cause a black portal to spawn at the location where Dusk was rescued, allowing the player to travel back in time, accessing the *Artorias of the Abyss* content.

Upon interaction with the portal, the hand of Manus reaches through time and pulls the player in a violent manner.

title: Broken Pendant
snippet:
Broken Pendant -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Half of a broken stone pendant. The vine appears to originate from Oolacile.

A powerful magic can be sensed from this ancient stone. Yet men of this time can neither manipulate nor sense its power, which has a distinct air consisting of both reverence and nostalgia.

title: Channeler
snippet:
Channeler -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Channelers** are enemies in *Dark Souls*.

title: Channeler
snippet:
Channeler -  Dark Souls - enemy - locations 
 locations : In the Undead Parish church, just before the Bell Gargoyles, on a ledge surrounded by sword-wielding Hollows. Does not respawn.
In the Depths above the Gaping Dragon boss entrance. This Channeler will buff the Gaping Dragon if he is not eliminated first, making the fight considerably harder. Does not respawn.
Three in The Duke's Archives. The first is located after the first lift. The other two are positioned in consecutive levels, above the bonfire on the balcony.

title: Channeler
snippet:
Channeler -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : If the player is equipped with a low damage weapon, it is advisable to wait, lure and stay away from their melee attack, and then hit them. Players might want to keep their shield raised as the Channeler's Trident can cover a surprising distance. If equipped with a higher damage weapon, such as the Gravelord Sword, rush the Channelers before they can attack.

At range, players can seek cover from the Channeler's soul arrow and either hit them with a ranged attack or advance and use the previous strategy.

If the Channeler has frenzied nearby enemies, players might want to focus on killing these first before targeting the Channeler, so they don't interfere.

The Channeler in the Undead Parish church can be sniped with a bow with impunity if far enough away.

title: Channeler
snippet:
Channeler -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : They appear slightly larger than the player, donning protective robes of peculiar design and utilizing a mystical Trident. Channelers are sorcerers who cast powerful Soul Arrows from afar. They can teleport away from harm and are invulnerable during the animation.

Channelers perform a unique martial arts dance that stirs nearby allies into a bloodthirsty frenzy,
greatly increasing their and their allies' damage output. Affected creatures display an aura of blue magic lines to indicate the active buff.

title: Channeler
snippet:
Channeler -  Dark Souls - enemy - attacks 
 attacks : Increases damage of user and nearby allies by x1.85.

Ascends +10 standard wpn to crystal weapon. (crystal weapons can be reinforced to +5)

Crystal weapons are powerful but brittle, and cannot be repaired once broken.

Crystal Golems are *phenomenally* resistant to magic damage. Trying to bring them down with sorceries, or weapons that do primarily magical damage (such as the Moonlight Butterfly Horn) is incredibly inefficient.

title: Fang Boar
snippet:
Fang Boar -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : The Fang Boar is a very large boar covered in steel plating and featuring enormous tusks. As such, most weapons tend to bounce off its armor. This plating doesn't cover the whole body of the boar in the Undead Parish, with the rear open to attacks and Backstabs. However the other two boars protecting the entrance to The Duke's Archives are completely armored and much more resistant, and cannot be Backstabbed.

Their charging attack is deflectable when parrying[https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Fang_Boar#Videos]. This is not a traditional parry, it is more redirecting the boar and leaving it momentarily in its recovery animation. You cannot use deflecting parry to Riposte the Boar, but it may give players time to circle around behind the Boar in Undead Parish for a Backstab.

title: Fang Boar
snippet:
Fang Boar -  Dark Souls - enemy - the_duke_s_archive 
 the_duke_s_archive : #The boars cannot leave The Duke's Archive, and can be lured towards the exit, where then the player can use ranged attacks to kill them.
#As the boars are no longer able to be backstabbed, the player can instead use Poison or Fire to deal damage, as they are weak to them. If this strategy is used with weapons that inflict one of the two, it will be better to use thrust weapons against them, as it doesn't cause the weapon to be deflected. Alternatively if no reliable thrust weapons are available, jump attacks also can not be deflected.
#Spells such as Sorceries, Pyromancies, and Miracles can be effective at bypassing their armor, which like most shields, is not as effective at blocking elemental damage as it is physical damage. This may however require precise timing, as most spells have high starting lag which can leave the player unable to evade attacks.

title: Fang Boar
snippet:
#The boars can easily be killed by running past them to beside the elevator. The boars can not run between the elevator and the pillar, thus allowing the player to kill them by range or melee.
#Some weapons can damage their unarmored underside with horizontal attacks. For example, Man-serpent sword's strong 2-handed attack deals full damage.

title: Lothric
snippet: The new inhabitants of the region soon found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. The old knights of Lothric turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, and built an altar for him in their city, beginning to worship the ancient deity who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Souls of Lords
snippet:
Souls of Lords -  Dark Souls - item - lore 
 lore : The Souls of Lords were discovered by the chosen few that "came from the dark". Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, Nito, the First of the Dead, The Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

Gwyn, Nito and The Witch of Izalith used the power procured from the Lord Souls to challenge the Everlasting Dragons for dominion of the world and, with the help of others, were successful in their endeavor.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate her own First Flame by using her Lord Soul, but this resulted in her own demise and the creation of the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons, who inherited possession of the Soul.

Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards are fragments of Gwyn's Lord Soul and were bestowed as gifts. One was given to Seath the Scaleless for betraying his own kind. Another was given to the Four Kings when Lord Gwyn recognized their foresight as leaders of New Londo.

title: Old Paledrake Soul
snippet:
Old Paledrake Soul -  Dark Souls II - item - trivia 
 trivia : This soul is likely a reference to Seath the Scaleless from *Dark Souls*.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Timeline -  Dark Souls III - storyline - before_time 
 before_time : Before the very existence of time itself the world is motionless, unformed and shrouded by fog.
Archtrees and the Everlasting Dragons, eternal and soulless beings similar to minerals, exist on the surface.

title: Gods
snippet:
At one point a God committed the sin of "greed". For this they were banished and cursed, resulting into their head transforming into an imitation of treasure chests. They became the very first Mimic. The Mimic became "the symbol of shame imposed on a long lost clan, exiled for the sin of avarice", perhaps meaning that this clan were similarly turned into Mimics.

Gwyn led the Gods and their Silver Knights in a war against the Dragons. With their powerful magic and the aid of the Dragon traitor, Seath the Scaleless, the Gods slew most of the Dragons and claimed the world for their own. Gwyn and his family founded the mighty city of Anor Londo, from whence they ruled over the humans, distant descendants of the Furtive Pygmy.

title: Dragon Torso Stone (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Dragon Torso Stone (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : A stone containing the strength of dragons.
Transforms the body into a roaring dragon, an effect that will remain until death.

The zealots who sought everlasting life are said to have conducted rites to imbue stones with the strength of dragons, but the truth of such claims is questionable.

title: Stone Dragon
snippet:
Stone Dragon -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Cut flying animations show that the Stone Dragon has legs and not a mass of tentacle-like appendages, unlike Seath the Scaleless.
According to an interview with Miyazaki, the Stone Dragon does not feel pain when its tail is cut off. The ancient dragons are half-living, half-element, and do not feel pain. The dragon depicted in the opening cutscene pre-dates the emergence of life in the world.
The Stone Dragon may be a Fire Keeper, considering that the nearby bonfire starts out lit and kindled.
